title: Finitely many elements of a separably generated extension lie in a finite separable extension of a finitely generated purely transcendental subfield
statement: Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] and let $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ be a transcendence basis of $K/k$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] such that $K$ is separable algebraic over the subfield $k(x_i;i\in I)\subseteq K$ generated by $k$ and all $x_i$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $n\ge0$ and $a_1,\dots,a_n\in K$. Then there is a finite subset $T\subseteq I$ with the following property: writing $L=k(x_i;i\in T)\subseteq K$ for the subfield generated by $k$ and the $x_i$ with $i\in T$, and $K'=L(a_1,\dots,a_n)\subseteq K$ for the subfield generated by $L$ and $a_1,\dots,a_n$, the extension $K'/L$ is finite (that is, $K'$ is a finite-dimensional $L$-vector space) and separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension].

proof.text: (The minimal polynomials and their Bezout identities.) Put $M=k(x_i;i\in I)\subseteq K$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis]. By hypothesis $K/M$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], so for each $j=1,\dots,n$ the element $a_j$ is algebraic over $M$ [def-weil-algebraic-element] and its minimal polynomial $P_j\in M[T]$ (monic, so nonzero; $M[T]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring]) is separable [def-pc-separable-polynomial]: there are $U_j,V_j\in M[T]$ with $U_jP_j+V_jP_j'=1$, $P_j'$ the formal derivative. Let $C\subseteq M$ be the set of all coefficients of all the $3n$ polynomials $P_j,U_j,V_j$; it is finite.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness), second paragraph, lines 10187-10191 (asserted without proof; argument written by the agent)

proof.text: (Choice of $T$.) Let $c\in C$. Since $c\in M=k(S)$ with $S=\{x_i:i\in I\}$, by [lem-weil-pbc-adjoin-element-finite-subset] (with $E_0=k$, $F=K$) there is a finite subset $S_c\subseteq S$ with $c\in k(S_c)$. Choose for each element of $S_c$ one index $i\in I$ with $x_i$ equal to it, and let $T_c\subseteq I$ be the finite set of chosen indices; then $S_c\subseteq\{x_i:i\in T_c\}$, so $k(S_c)\subseteq k(x_i;i\in T_c)$ (the latter is a subfield containing $k$ and $S_c$, and $k(S_c)$ is the smallest such), hence $c\in k(x_i;i\in T_c)$. Put $T=\bigcup_{c\in C}T_c$, a finite subset of $I$ ($C$ is finite), and $L=k(x_i;i\in T)$. For each $c$, $L$ is a subfield containing $k$ and all $x_i$ with $i\in T_c$, so $k(x_i;i\in T_c)\subseteq L$ and $c\in L$. Thus $C\subseteq L$ (for $n=0$, $C=\emptyset$ and $T=\emptyset$, $L=k$). Likewise $L\subseteq M$, as $M$ contains $k$ and all $x_i$, $i\in T$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness), second paragraph, lines 10187-10191 (asserted without proof; argument written by the agent)

proof.text: (Each $a_j$ is separable algebraic over $L$.) As $L\subseteq M$, the polynomial ring $L[T]$ is a subring of $M[T]$, and the formal derivative of a polynomial with coefficients in $L$ is the same computed in $L[T]$ or in $M[T]$. By step 2, $P_j,U_j,V_j$ lie in $L[T]$, and the identity $U_jP_j+V_jP_j'=1$ holds in $L[T]$ (it holds in $M[T]\supseteq L[T]$). So $P_j\in L[T]$ is separable [def-pc-separable-polynomial], nonzero, and $P_j(a_j)=0$; hence $a_j$ is algebraic over $L$ [def-weil-algebraic-element]. Let $\mu_j\in L[T]$ be the minimal polynomial of $a_j$ over $L$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]; it generates the kernel of $L[T]\to K$, $T\mapsto a_j$, which contains $P_j$, so $P_j=\mu_jR$ with $R\in L[T]$. Then $P_j'=\mu_j'R+\mu_jR'$ and $1=U_j\mu_jR+V_j(\mu_j'R+\mu_jR')=(U_jR+V_jR')\mu_j+(V_jR)\mu_j'$, so $\mu_j$ is separable, i.e. $a_j$ is separable over $L$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. The minimal polynomial is the same whether $a_j$ is viewed in $K$ or in the subfield $K'\ni a_j$ (the kernel of $L[T]\to K'$ equals that of $L[T]\to K$, since $K'\to K$ is injective), so $a_j$ is also algebraic and separable over $L$ as an element of $K'$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness), second paragraph, lines 10187-10191 (asserted without proof; argument written by the agent)

proof.text: ($K'/L$ is finite and algebraic.) By step 3, $a_1,\dots,a_n\in K$ are algebraic over $L$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] (with $k=L$, $\Omega=K$) the subfield $K'=L(a_1,\dots,a_n)\subseteq K$ is a finite-dimensional $L$-vector space, of dimension $d$ say. Every $\beta\in K'$ is then algebraic over $L$ [def-weil-algebraic-element]: the $d+1$ elements $1,\beta,\dots,\beta^d$ are $L$-linearly dependent, and a nontrivial relation $\sum_{e=0}^d\lambda_e\beta^e=0$ is a nonzero polynomial $\sum_e\lambda_eT^e\in L[T]$ vanishing at $\beta$. So $K'/L$ is an algebraic extension [def-pc-field-extension].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness), second paragraph, lines 10187-10191 (asserted without proof; argument written by the agent)

proof.text: ($K'/L$ is separable algebraic.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable] to the algebraic extension $K'/L$ (step 4): the separable algebraic closure $K'_s\subseteq K'$ of $L$ in $K'$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure], the set of elements of $K'$ separable over $L$, is a subfield of $K'$ containing $L$, and $K'_s/L$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. By step 3 every $a_j$ lies in $K'_s$. So $K'_s$ is a subfield of $K$ containing $L$ and $a_1,\dots,a_n$; since $K'=L(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ is the smallest such subfield, $K'\subseteq K'_s\subseteq K'$, so $K'_s=K'$ and $K'/L$ is separable algebraic. Together with step 4, $K'/L$ is finite and separable algebraic, as claimed.
